newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: ATHLETICS-COMMONWEALTH GAMES SCHEDULE PUT BACK TWO DAYS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-COMMONWEALTH GAMES SCHEDULE PUT BACK TWO DAYS.

text.p: Commonwealth Games organisers have put back the 1998 Kuala Lumpur Games' athletics schedule by two days to avoid a clash with the Johannesburg World Cup.

At a news conference on Thursday, International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) president Primo Nebiolo said the Games' programme would now start on September 16, three days after the conclusion of the three-day World Cup.
"I am extremely happy," Nebiolo said. "Our athletes will travel on Monday, September 14, arrive in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday and on Wednesday, September 16 they will compete."

The Commonwealth Games' Federation's (CMF), who had originally planned to start the athletics' schedule on September 14, found their hand forced when Nebiolo announced last month that the World Cup would be staged from September 11-13.
Nebiolo said at the time that the World Cup had to take priority over the Games and added: "The Commonwealth Games cannot occupy any window. Who is leading athletics around the world?"
In a letter to the IAAF dated October 7, CMF chairman Michael Fennell acknowledged there was a problem and suggested starting the Games athletics programme on September 16.
In reply Nebiolo said the IAAF had considered the CMF's suggestion at its annual calendar meeting here and accepted the proposal.
"We have a great appreciation of the Commonwealth Games because the Commonwealth Games is a great event and because it gives great propaganda for athletics," he told the news conference.
"We have found a splendid agreement so our athletes will be in Johannesburg for the World Cup and three days after they will compete in the Commonwealth Games."
